form_analysis.feedback: Excellent and necessary aftercare for a more intense modality. Clearly distinguishes between therapeutic soreness and problematic pain. Provides specific, practical protocols for inflammation management (contrast therapy, Epsom salts) and clear red flags. Manages patient expectations effectively.

form_data.introduction: This aftercare advice is CRUCIAL following your deep tissue massage. This technique works on deeper muscle layers and fascia, which can lead to a therapeutic inflammatory response. Proper aftercare manages this response, reduces discomfort, and enhances the long-term benefits.

instructions.general_directive: Please follow these instructions carefully to support your body's healing process.

sections.title: Expected Post-Treatment Sensations and Timeline
sections.content: It is NORMAL to feel muscle soreness, similar to that after a rigorous workout, for 24-72 hours after treatment. This is often described as a 'good hurt' in the targeted areas. The peak of soreness is typically 24-48 hours post-massage. Stiffness is also common. This is part of the healing process as muscles release chronic tension.

sections.title: Managing Soreness and Inflammation
items: Contrast Therapy: For areas of significant soreness, apply a cycle of heat and cold. Use a warm compress or heating pad for 3-4 minutes to increase blood flow, then a cold pack for 1-2 minutes to reduce inflammation. Repeat 2-3 times.
Epsom Salt Bath: A warm (not hot) bath with 2 cups of Epsom salts (magnesium sulfate) can be immensely soothing and help reduce muscle aches. Soak for 15-20 minutes.
Hydration: Drink EXTRA water for the next 48-72 hours. This is vital to flush metabolic byproducts and prevent excessive soreness.
Gentle Movement: Do NOT remain sedentary. Light walking, gentle stretching, and range-of-motion exercises will help prevent stiffness and promote circulation. Avoid strenuous exercise for 48 hours.

sections.title: Pain vs. Soreness - Red Flags
sections.content: SORENESS is a dull, aching, generalized feeling. PAIN is sharp, acute, or shooting. You should NOT experience: Sharp nerve pain, numbness or tingling that persists, increased joint pain, or intense pain that limits normal movement. If you experience these, contact your therapist.

sections.title: Medication and Supplement Guidance
sections.content: If you are comfortable taking them, over-the-counter anti-inflammatory medication (like Ibuprofen) can help manage soreness. Natural anti-inflammatories like turmeric or tart cherry juice may also be beneficial. Avoid alcohol for 24 hours as it increases inflammation and dehydration.

sections.title: Follow-Up and Integration
sections.content: The benefits of deep tissue work integrate over several days. You may notice improved range of motion and decreased pain in the treated areas as soreness subsides. It may take 2-3 sessions to fully address a chronic issue.

sections.title: When to Contact Your Therapist
items: If soreness is severe and not improving after 72 hours.
If you experience any of the 'red flag' pain symptoms mentioned above.
If you have bruising that is extensive or painful (some minor bruising can be normal).
To provide feedback on pressure and areas of focus for your next session.

sections.title: General Side Effects and Results Assessment
items: Minor bruising is possible and will fade in 3-7 days. Arnica cream or gel can be helpful.
The therapeutic release and alignment benefits become most apparent 2-3 days post-treatment, once initial soreness fades.
Regular sessions (e.g., every 2-4 weeks) are often needed to break chronic holding patterns.
